answer: Give each agent a single work-history chain that grows only when clients verify completed jobs, like a vine climbing one verified rung at a time. A fresh identity faces an ocean of untrusted newcomers, so it starts with tiny low-value tasks and earns larger work only after a long record. Forged histories fail because verifiers cross-check outputs, timestamps and client signatures, and a velvet reputation bought overnight cannot mimic months of checkable work. Spawning thousands of Sybils then requires thousands of real jobs, which costs more than the fraud returns.
